summary: Musashi Tachikawa specializes in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He earned degrees from Nagoya University and a Ph.D. from Harvard under Daniel H. H. Ingalls. He held positions at Nagoya University, National Museum of Ethnology, and Aichi Gakuin University (~2005–2012).

Muzaffar Alam works in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Jamia Millia Islamia, Aligarh Muslim University, and Jawaharlal Nehru University, where he taught from ~1973 to 2001. Around 2001, he joined the University of Chicago as Bobrinskoy Professor.

Myles Dillon worked in linguistics and Indology, studying at University College Dublin and in Europe under scholars including Osborn Bergin and Rudolf Thurneysen. He held posts at Trinity College Dublin, UCD, the University of Wisconsin-Madison, and directed DIAS (1960–1968).
Myokyo-ni was a Buddhist studies scholar. She studied at the University of Graz and underwent traditional training under Soko Morinaga in 1984.
Myosei Tatsuguchi is a Buddhist studies scholar who served as a professor at Ryukoku University (attested in 1987) and later became professor emeritus there (attested in 2015).

Mysore Hiriyanna was a scholar of philosophy, Indology, and religious studies. He studied at Madras Christian College under Perisamy Tirumalacharya and Kashi Sesharamasastry, later serving as Professor of Sanskrit at Maharaja's College and the University of Mysore (~1917–1927).

Mysore Narasimhachar Srinivas studied at the University of Mysore, University of Mumbai, and University of Oxford. A specialist in Indology, he held appointments at Oxford, MS University of Baroda, and University of Delhi, and chaired the ISEC (1972–1979).

Mónika Kiss is a scholar in Japanology and Buddhist studies. She pursued doctoral studies at Eötvös Loránd University under the supervision of Masanori Yamaji, also studying under Robert F. Rhodes and Nozomu Saito.
N. A. Gore was an Indologist who served as Librarian at the Asiatic Society of Mumbai (attested 1957–1958) and Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar Marathwada University (attested 1967).

N. A. Jayawickrama worked in Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics. He served as a professor at the University of Ceylon (attested 1974) and at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies.

N. Aiyaswami Sastri was a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies who studied at Madras Sanskrit College and Visva-Bharati University. He held professorships at Sri Venkateswara Oriental College (attested 1940) and Visva-Bharati University (attested 1971).
N. D. Mironov was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at the University of Leipzig (~1902–1903) under Hermann Jacobi and also studied under Heinrich Hübschmann.
N. J. Karthika is a scholar in computational fields and Indology. She completed her Ph.D. at the Indian Institute of Technology Bombay and also held a post there.

N. Lakshminarayana Rao was an Indologist and epigraphist. He served as Government Epigraphist for India at the Archaeological Survey of India and was appointed Special Officer (Epigraphy) by the Government of India in 1956.
N. R. Bhatt was an Indology scholar who held positions at the French Institute of Pondicherry and was a member of the École française d'Extrême-Orient (attested 1966).

N. S. Ramachandra Murthy worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He served as Epigraphy Assistant at the Department of Archaeology and Museums, Andhra Pradesh, and retired as Professor of Indian History and Archaeology at Sri Venkateswara University.

N. S. Ramanuja Tatacharya specialized in Indology and philosophy. He served as Vice Chancellor of National Sanskrit University (1989–1994) and was a researcher at the French Institute of Pondicherry (~1994–2017).
N. Taher is an archaeologist who served as the head of the Bhopal circle at the Archaeological Survey of India, where he succeeded K. K. Muhammed.

N. Veezhinathan, a scholar of Indology and philosophy, earned his Ph.D. from Savitribai Phule Pune University in 1964 under A. Sankaran. He worked as a Research Scholar at Deccan College (1960–1963) and became Lecturer at the University of Madras in 1964.

N. Venkataramanayya was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology who studied under Ferrand E. Corley. He served as Reader in Indian History at the University of Madras (attested 1957) and Deputy Director for Epigraphy in Andhra Pradesh.
